page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server designed for high-performance computing workloads. It features 48 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz, with one thread per core. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 150 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the hpc7a.24xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance, particularly in multi-core processing and memory bandwidth. It achieves top 10% placement in multi-core CPU stress tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and software compilation with Clang. Large-block memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 695.05 GB/sec for read operations and 347.3 GB/sec for write operations. Single-core performance and cryptographic operations also rank in the top 25%, while web serving throughput and single-threaded compression remain in the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive parallel computing due to its massive DDR5 memory allocation and high-speed baseline networking. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware represents a clear tradeoff, making it less suitable for local-storage-heavy databases or GPU-accelerated deep learning. It is highly optimized for workloads such as high-performance computing (HPC), large-scale software compilation, molecular modeling, physics simulations, and memory-bound parallel processing.
